a13.salok: Salok. Whoever comes to the refuge of a Sant (a saint) is saved. Nanak, by slandering a Sant one is born again and again.
a13.p1: Ashtapadi. By slandering a Sant, one's life is cut short. By slandering a Sant, one is not freed from the Messenger of Death. By slandering a Sant, all peace departs. By slandering a Sant, one falls into hell. By slandering a Sant, the intellect becomes defiled. By slandering a Sant, one is left without honour. No one can protect one whom a Sant has cast off. By slandering a Sant, one falls from one's place. If the compassionate Sant shows grace, then, Nanak, in the company of the Sants even the slanderer crosses over.
a13.p2: By slandering a Sant, one's face becomes twisted. By slandering the Sants, one caws like a crow. By slandering the Sants, one is born as a snake. By slandering a Sant, one is born among crawling creatures and wriggles like a worm. By slandering the Sants, one burns in craving. By slandering a Sant, one deceives everyone. By slandering a Sant, all one's radiance departs. By slandering a Sant, one becomes the lowest of the low. One who maligns a Sant has no resting place at all. Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, even they attain salvation.
a13.p3: The slanderer of a Sant is a great evildoer. The slanderer of a Sant finds no rest even for a moment. The slanderer of a Sant is a great murderer. The slanderer of a Sant is struck down by the Transcendent Lord. The slanderer of a Sant is stripped of sovereignty. The slanderer of a Sant is miserable and wretched. The slanderer of a Sant suffers every disease. The slanderer of a Sant lives in separation for ever. Slandering a Sant is the sin above all sins. Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, even he is liberated.
a13.p4: One who maligns a Sant is ever impure. One who maligns a Sant is no one's friend. One who maligns a Sant is punished. One who maligns a Sant is abandoned by all. One who maligns a Sant is utterly proud. One who maligns a Sant is ever given to vice. One who maligns a Sant is born and dies. Through slander of a Sant, one strays from peace. One who maligns a Sant has no place to stand. Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, even he is brought into union.
a13.p5: One who maligns a Sant breaks down halfway. One who maligns a Sant reaches the end of no task. One who maligns a Sant is made to wander in the wilderness. One who maligns a Sant is led off into desolate places. One who maligns a Sant is hollow within, like the body of the dead without breath. One who maligns a Sant has no root at all; such people themselves eat what they themselves have sown. One who maligns a Sant has no one else to protect him. Nanak, if it pleases the Sant, even he is rescued.
a13.p6: One who maligns a Sant cries out in pain, as a fish writhes without water. One who maligns a Sant stays hungry and is never filled, as fire is never sated by fuel. One who maligns a Sant is left all alone, like a barren sesame stalk, forlorn in the field. One who maligns a Sant is without dharma (righteousness). One who maligns a Sant ever speaks lies. The slanderer's lot, shaped by his deeds, was set from the very start. Nanak, whatever pleases the Lord, that alone comes to pass.
a13.p7: One who maligns a Sant becomes deformed. One who maligns a Sant is punished in the Lord's court. One who maligns a Sant is kept ever in agony. One who maligns a Sant neither dies nor is allowed to live. The hopes of one who maligns a Sant are never fulfilled. One who maligns a Sant rises and departs in despair. By maligning a Sant, no one is ever satisfied. As it pleases the Lord, so a person becomes. No one can erase the record of deeds once it is written. Nanak, the True One alone knows.
a13.p8: All hearts are his; he is the Doer. For ever and ever, bow to him. Sing God's praise day and night. With each breath and each mouthful, meditate on him. Everything that happens is his doing. As he makes a person, so that person becomes. He himself is the player of his own play. Who else could offer counsel? To whom he shows grace, he gives his own Naam (the Name). Very fortunate, Nanak, are those humble servants.
a14.salok: Salok. Give up your cleverness, O good people, and remember in Simran (meditative remembrance) the Lord, the King. Keep in your mind the hope of the one Lord alone; Nanak, then pain, doubt and fear depart.
a14.p1: Ashtapadi. Know that all reliance on human beings is in vain. The one Lord God alone is the Giver. By his gifts one remains satisfied, and craving does not come to cling again. He alone kills and preserves. Nothing is in human hands. By understanding his Hukam (will), one finds peace. Keep his Naam (Name) strung around your neck. Remember, remember, remember that God. Nanak, then no obstacle will touch you.
a14.p2: In your mind, praise the Formless Lord. O my mind, carry on true dealings. With a pure tongue drink the nectar, and make your soul ever at peace. With your eyes behold the play of the Master. In the Saadh Sangat (the congregation of the holy), all other attachments fade away. With your feet walk on the path of Gobind. Sins are erased by meditating on the Lord even for a moment. With your hands do the Lord's work, and with your ears listen to the story of the Lord. Nanak, then in the Lord's court your forehead shines bright.
a14.p3: Fortunate in the world are those people who sing the virtues of the Lord for ever and ever. Those who reflect on the Lord's Name are counted wealthy in the world. Those who speak of the Lord, the Most High, with mind, body and mouth: know that they are at peace for ever and ever. One who recognises the One, and only the One, has the understanding of this world and the next. One whose mind is at one with the Naam, Nanak, has known the Immaculate Lord.
a14.p4: One who, by the Guru's grace, comes to understand his own self: know that his craving is quenched. One who speaks the praises of the Lord in the Saadh Sangat, that servant of the Lord stays free of all disease. One who night and day utters only Kirtan, the praise of God, he alone is free of attachment while living as a householder. The person whose hope rests on the One alone has the noose of Death cut away. One who hungers in his mind for the Supreme Lord, Nanak, no sorrows cling to him.
a14.p5: One into whose mind and consciousness the Lord God comes, that Sant (saint) is at peace and does not waver. One upon whom his God shows grace, tell me, whom should that servant fear? He has been seen just as he is; he himself pervades his own creation. Searching, searching, searching, I have succeeded; by the Guru's grace I have understood the whole essence. Whenever I look, everything I see is the Root, the source of all. Nanak, he is the subtle, and he is the tangible.
a14.p6: Nothing is born and nothing dies; he alone performs his own play. Coming and going, the seen and the unseen: the whole creation he has made obedient. He himself is all in all; he himself is in all. In many ways he creates, establishes and uproots. He is imperishable; nothing of him is ever broken. He gives his support and holds up the universe. The Being, unseen and unfathomable, is glorious. Nanak, if he himself makes one chant, then one chants.
a14.p7: Those who have known God are glorious; the whole world is saved by their teaching. God's servants save all. God's servants dispel sorrow. The merciful Lord himself unites them with himself; chanting the Guru's Shabad (Word), they are filled with bliss. He alone comes to serve them, the fortunate one on whom they bestow grace. Chanting the Naam, they find rest. Nanak, regard those persons as the most exalted.
a14.p8: Whatever such a servant does, he does in God's love. For ever and ever he dwells with the Lord. Whatever happens, happens in its natural course; he recognises that one Doer. What God does seems sweet to his servant. God is seen just as he is. From whom they sprang, into him they merge. They become treasures of peace; this state befits them alone. He himself has given honour to himself. Nanak, know God and his servant to be one.
a15.salok: Salok. God is full of every power and knows all pain. By remembering him in Simran (meditative remembrance) one is saved; Nanak is a sacrifice to him.
a15.p1: Ashtapadi. Gopal, the Sustainer of the world, mends what is broken. He himself cherishes all beings. He who holds the care of all in his mind, from him no one goes away empty-handed. O my mind, ever chant the Lord. God, the Imperishable, is himself all in all. Nothing happens by one's own doing, even if a mortal longs for it a hundred times. Apart from him, nothing can serve your purpose. Nanak, salvation comes by chanting the Name of the one Lord.
a15.p2: Being beautiful, let no one be vain; it is God's light that adorns every heart. Being wealthy, why should anyone be proud, when all wealth is his gift? If someone calls himself a great hero, without God's power where can he run? If someone sets himself up as a giver, the Giver knows him to be a fool. One whose sickness of Haumai (ego) is broken by the Guru's grace, Nanak, that person is ever healthy.
a15.p3: As a pillar holds up a building, so the Guru's Shabad (Word) is the mainstay of the mind. As a stone crosses over aboard a boat, so the mortal who clings to the Guru's feet is carried across. As a lamp brings light to darkness, so by beholding the Guru, the mind blossoms. As one finds the path in a great wilderness, so by joining the company of the Saadh (the holy one), the inner light shines forth. I long for the dust of the feet of those Sants (saints). O Lord, fulfil Nanak's longing.
a15.p4: O foolish mind, why do you wail? What was written long ago is what one receives. Pain and pleasure are given by God; leave all others and keep him in mind. Whatever he does, accept it as happiness. Why do you wander astray, ignorant one? What thing came with you? You are caught up in pleasures like a greedy moth. Chant the Lord's Name in your heart. Nanak, then you will go home with honour.
a15.p5: The merchandise you came to buy, the Lord's Name, is found in the house of the Sants. Give up pride, O mind, and buy it; weigh the Lord's Name in your heart. Load this cargo and travel with the Sants; give up all other snares of poisonous Maya (worldly attachment). Everyone calls such a one blessed, blessed, and his face is radiant in the Lord's court. Only a rare one trades in this trade. Nanak is ever a sacrifice to such a one.
a15.p6: Wash the feet of the Saadh again and again, and drink that water. Offer your soul to the Saadh. Bathe in the dust of the Saadh. Give yourself as a sacrifice to the Saadh. Service of the Saadh comes through great fortune. In the Saadh Sangat (the congregation of the holy), people sing the Lord's Kirtan (sung praise). The Saadh keeps one safe from many obstacles. Singing the Lord's virtues, one tastes the nectar. One who took the shelter of the Sants and came to their door, Nanak, has gained every comfort.
a15.p7: He brings the dead to life. He gives sustenance to the hungry. All treasures lie within his glance; people receive the share written for them beforehand. Everything is his; he is able to do all. Besides him there has been no other, nor will there be. Chant, O humble one, for ever and ever, day and night; this is the highest and purest deed of all. One to whom he graciously gave the Naam (the Name), Nanak, that person became pure.
a15.p8: One in whose mind there is faith in the Guru, into that person's consciousness the Lord God comes. He is heard of in the three worlds as a devotee, a devotee, in whose heart is the One alone. True are his deeds, true is his way of life; truth is in his heart, and truth he speaks with his mouth. His vision is true, and to him all form is true; truth prevails, and true is the whole expanse. One who has known the Supreme Lord as true, Nanak, that person merges into the True One.
a16.salok: Salok. He has no form, no outline, no colour at all; God is beyond the three qualities (gunas). Nanak, he gives understanding to the one with whom he is well pleased.
a16.p1: Ashtapadi. Keep the Imperishable God in your mind. Give up your love for human beings. Beyond him there is nothing and no one; the One alone is present within all. He himself is all-seeing, he himself all-knowing; deep, profound, unfathomable and all-wise. He is the Supreme Lord, the Transcendent Lord, Gobind; the treasure of mercy, compassionate and forgiving. May I fall at the feet of your Saadhs (holy ones): this is the longing in Nanak's mind.
a16.p2: He fulfils desires and is able to give refuge. What he has ordained comes to pass. In the blink of his eye he destroys and replenishes; no one else knows his secret counsel. He is the embodiment of bliss, and rejoicing is ever in his house; all things are said to be in his house. In kingship he is the king, in Yoga the yogi; in austerity the great ascetic, in household life the enjoyer. Meditating on him again and again, the devotees have found peace. Nanak, no one has found the limit of that Being.
a16.p3: His play has no limit; all the gods have grown weary plumbing it. What does a son know of his father's birth? He has strung all upon his own thread. Those to whom he gives good understanding, wisdom and meditation, those servants and slaves of his meditate on the Naam (the Name). Those whom he makes wander in the three qualities are born and die, and come and go again and again. The high places and the low are all his. Nanak, as he makes one know, so one knows.
a16.p4: Many are his forms, many his colours; he takes on many guises, yet is of one hue. In many ways he has made the expanse: God, the imperishable, the One (Ekankaar). In an instant he stages many plays; the Perfect One fills every place. In many ways he has fashioned the creation; his own worth he alone knows. Every heart is his, every place is his. Nanak lives by chanting and chanting the Lord's Name.
a16.p5: Upheld by the Naam are all creatures. Upheld by the Naam are the worlds and universes. Upheld by the Naam are the Simritis, the Vedas and the Puranas. Upheld by the Naam are listening, wisdom and meditation. Upheld by the Naam are the skies and the nether worlds. Upheld by the Naam are all forms. Upheld by the Naam are the realms and all the worlds. Through the Naam, by hearing it with their ears, people have been saved. One whom he graciously attaches to his own Naam, Nanak, that person attains salvation in the fourth state (beyond the three qualities).
a16.p6: His form is true, his place is true. True is the Being, he alone supreme. His deeds are true, his word (Bani) is true. The True Being is contained in all. True is his grace, true his creation. True is the root, and true is what springs from it. True is his doing, the purest of the pure. One whom he makes understand finds it all good. True is the Name of God, the giver of peace. Nanak, true faith is received from the Guru.
a16.p7: True is the word, the teaching of the Saadh. True are the people in whose hearts it comes to dwell. If anyone comes to understand love for the True One, by chanting the Naam he attains salvation. He is true himself, and true is everything he has made. His own measure and state he alone knows. Whose creation it is, he is its maker. No one else understands it or gives thought to it. The Creator's limit is not known by what he has created. Nanak, whatever pleases him comes to pass.
a16.p8: Wondering at his wonder, one is struck with awe. Whoever has understood this has come to taste its relish. God's servants remain steeped in his love; through the Guru's word they have gained the priceless treasures. They are givers and removers of pain; in their company the world crosses over. The servant of such a servant is very fortunate; in the company of such a servant, one's mind is fixed in love on the One. That servant sings Kirtan (sung praise) of the virtues of Gobind. By the Guru's grace, Nanak, he gains the fruit.
a17.salok: Salok. True in the beginning, true at the start of the ages; true he is now, and, Nanak, true he will ever be.
a17.p1: Ashtapadi. His feet are true, and those who touch them are true. His worship is true, and those who serve him are true. The sight of him is true, and those who behold it are true. His Naam (Name) is true, and those who meditate on it are true. He himself is true, and all that he upholds is true. He himself is virtue, and he himself bestows virtue. His Shabad (Word) is true, and the one who speaks of God is true. The attention is true, and the one who listens to his praise is true. To one who understands, all is true. Nanak, true, true is that God.
a17.p2: One who has believed in his heart in the Embodiment of Truth has recognised the Doer, the One who causes all to be done, as the root. One into whose heart faith in God has come, in his mind the essence of wisdom is revealed. Passing from fear to fearlessness, he dwells there; he merges into the One from whom he sprang. When one thing is taken and blended into its own substance, it can no longer be called separate. One with understanding understands this discernment. Nanak, meeting the Lord, he becomes one with him.
a17.p3: The Master's servant is obedient. The Master's servant ever worships him. In the mind of the Master's servant there is faith. Pure is the way of life of the Master's servant. The servant knows the Master to be with him. God's servant is steeped in the love of the Naam. God is the one who sustains his servant. The Formless Lord keeps his servant's honour. He alone is a servant on whom God bestows mercy. Nanak, such a servant remembers him with every breath.
a17.p4: He covers the faults of his own servant. He surely protects his own servant. He gives greatness to his own slave. He makes his own servant chant the Naam. He himself guards his own servant's honour. No one can perceive that servant's state and stature. No one can equal God's servant. God's servants are the highest of the high. One whom God has set to his own service, Nanak, that servant is made known in all ten directions.
a17.p5: He places power in a tiny ant, and it reduces armies of millions upon millions to ashes. One whose breath he himself does not take away, him he protects, giving him his hand. A person makes efforts of many kinds, but his efforts go in vain. No one else kills or preserves; he alone is the protector of all beings. Why do you worry, O mortal? Nanak, chant God, the Unseen, the Wondrous.
a17.p6: Again and again and again, one should chant God. Drinking the nectar, this mind and body are sated. One who as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) has gained the jewel of the Naam sees nothing else. The Naam is his wealth, the Naam his beauty and delight. The Naam is his peace, the Lord's Name his companion. Those who are satisfied with the relish of the Naam have their minds and bodies absorbed in the Naam alone. Rising, sitting, sleeping, the Naam: says Nanak, this is ever the occupation of the Lord's servant.
a17.p7: Speak his praise with your tongue day and night. God has bestowed this gift on his servants. They perform devotional worship with the eagerness of their soul, and remain absorbed in their God. Such a one knows what has been and what is coming to be. He recognises the Hukam (will) of his God. How could I describe the glory of such a one? I do not know how to tell even one of his virtues. Those who dwell all twenty-four hours in God's presence, says Nanak, are the perfect ones.
a17.p8: O my mind, take their shelter; give your mind and body to those servants. The servant who has recognised his God is the giver of all things. In his refuge you will find every comfort; through the sight of him you will be rid of all sins. Give up all other cleverness; devote yourself to the service of that servant. Your coming and going will end. Nanak, worship the feet of that servant for ever.
a18.salok: Salok. One who has known the True Being, his name is Satguru (the True Guru). Through his company the Sikh is saved; Nanak, sing the virtues of the Lord.
a18.p1: Ashtapadi. The Satguru cherishes the Sikh. The Guru is ever merciful to his servant. The Guru removes the filth of the Sikh's evil thinking. Through the Guru's words, the Sikh utters the Lord's Name. The Satguru cuts the Sikh's bonds. The Guru's Sikh turns away from vice. The Satguru gives the Sikh the wealth of the Naam (the Name). The Guru's Sikh is truly fortunate. The Satguru makes good the Sikh's life here and hereafter. Nanak, the Satguru cares for the Sikh with all his heart.
a18.p2: The servant who lives in the Guru's house accepts the Guru's command in his mind. He does not make himself out to be anyone. He ever meditates on the Lord's Name in his heart. One who sells his mind to the Satguru, that servant's affairs come right. One who serves without desire for reward attains the Master. One on whom he himself bestows his grace, Nanak, that servant takes the Guru's teaching.
a18.p3: One who accepts the Guru's will wholly, in full measure, that servant comes to understand the state of the Transcendent Lord. He is the Satguru in whose heart is the Lord's Name. I offer myself to the Guru as a sacrifice, many times over. He is the giver of all treasures and of life. All twenty-four hours he is steeped in the love of the Supreme Lord. The servant is in God, and the Supreme Lord is in the servant. He himself is One; of this there is no doubt. By a thousand clevernesses he cannot be won. Nanak, such a Guru is found by great good fortune.
a18.p4: Fruitful is the sight of him; beholding him, one becomes pure. Touching his feet, one's state and way of life become pure. Meeting him in his company, one dwells on the virtues of the Lord, and reaches the court of the Supreme Lord. Hearing his words, the ears are filled. Contentment comes into the mind, and the soul is at rest. Perfect is the Guru, everlasting his teaching. One upon whom he looks with his nectar glance becomes a Sant (saint). Endless are his virtues; his worth cannot be assessed. Nanak, whoever pleases him, him he unites with himself.
a18.p5: One tongue, and his praises are many. The True Being is perfect in discernment. No mortal's words can reach him. God is unreachable, beyond the senses, free of all attachment. He needs no food, has no enmity, and is the giver of peace; no one has found his worth. Countless devotees bow to him daily. They remember his lotus feet in their hearts. I am ever a sacrifice to my Satguru. Nanak, by his grace such a God is meditated upon.
a18.p6: Only a rare person obtains this essence of the Lord. One who drinks the nectar becomes immortal. That person never perishes in whose mind the Treasure of virtues is revealed. All twenty-four hours he takes the Lord's Name. He gives true teaching to his servant. He is not stained by attachment to Maya (worldly illusion). He keeps the one Lord in his mind. In the darkness a lamp has given light. Nanak, doubt, attachment and pain have fled from there.
a18.p7: In the burning heat, coolness has spread. Bliss has come, and the pains have fled, O brother. The anxieties of birth and death are gone through the perfect teachings of the Saadh (the holy one). Fear is ended, and they dwell fearless; all ailments are destroyed and have fled from the mind. The One whose own they were has shown grace. In the Saadh Sangat (the congregation of the holy), chant the Name of Murari, the Lord. Stability is found and the wandering of doubt is ended, Nanak, by hearing with the ears the praises of the Lord.
a18.p8: He himself is beyond all qualities (Nirgun), and he is also with qualities (Sargun). Assuming his power, he has enchanted the whole creation. God himself has made his own wondrous plays. He alone knows his own worth. Besides the Lord there is no other. The One alone is present within all. Through and through he pervades all forms and colours. He is revealed in the company of the Saadh. Having made the creation, he has placed his own power within it. Many times over, Nanak is a sacrifice to him.
